title: Saltimbocca alla Romana
subtitle: Roman veal with prosciutto and sage
excerpt: Thin veal escalopes with a slice of prosciutto and a sage leaf pressed to each one, pan-fried and finished in white wine. The whole dish is on the table in 20 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Saltimbocca alla romana (literally 'jump in the mouth') is a dish firmly rooted in the trattoria cooking of Rome. It appears in numerous Italian cookery books of the twentieth century, including Ada Boni's La cucina romana.

recipeTools.notes: A large flat pan to fit the escalopes without overlapping.

content.text: Saltimbocca is thin veal escalopes each topped with a slice of prosciutto and a sage leaf, cooked quickly in butter and finished with a splash of white wine. The prosciutto goes crisp, the sage fries golden, and the whole thing takes minutes. It is one of those Roman restaurant dishes that is actually very simple at home.

Lay the veal flat. Place a slice of prosciutto on each escalope and press two sage leaves on top. Secure with a cocktail stick if they seem likely to slip. Season lightly on the veal side only. Dust the veal side with a little flour.

Heat the butter in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat until foaming. Place the escalopes prosciutto-side down. Cook for 2 minutes until the prosciutto is crisp. Flip and cook the veal side for 1 minute.

Pour the white wine into the pan and let it bubble fiercely for about 1 minute, tilting the pan to coat the meat. The sauce will reduce to a light glaze. Remove the cocktail sticks and serve immediately.
